content.thinking:
I need to write this whole file carefully in one pass since I can't test it, designing a roughly 3-meter lava golem in Genshin-style cel-shading with gold filigree and a pyro glow. I'm sketching the skeleton structure: hips as root, spine chain rising to chest, neck, and head, with arms running through shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fist joints, and legs through hip, knee, and ankle.

Now I'm working out the color palette and body-building structure—cel-shaded basalt tones for the body with lighter plate highlights, magma orange-gold glows for emissive cracks, and gold accents, making sure glow parts use flat colors rather than paint functions. I'm building out the joint chains using catmull-spline paths for the spine and neck, carefully matching point counts to name arrays so each segment gets labeled correctly.

I'm sketching proportions: hips at 1.25m, chest top around 2.35m, shoulders at 2.2m width ±0.75m, head center near 2.6m, and overall height roughly 3.0-3.3m including a crest. Now I'm setting up the head as a separate joint parented to the neck chain, and starting to loft the torso using the spine chain as the bone reference.

Working out torso station widths and heights at pelvis, waist, and chest, and figuring out how the loft's cross-section axes (width and depth) align relative to the upward-facing spine path.

Now I'm planning the chest detail: scattering basalt plate boxes across the torso surface using a normal-direction filter, and adding a molten emissive core sphere with a gold torus ring positioned near the front of the chest.

I'm also planning thin glowing orange seam sweeps draped across the torso surface using catmull curves to simulate molten cracks, then moving on to the arm geometry.

For the arms, I'm defining each side's chain as shoulder, elbow, and wrist points with slight outward separation for a natural resting pose, naming each joint per side so the limb segments can be built between them.

Now I'm sketching the shoulder pauldron as a bulky lump attached near the shoulder joint, using varying radii to taper the arm from a thick upper section down to a slimmer wrist, with basalt-toned coloring applied across the limb.

Still planning joint placement...

For the legs I'm setting up the chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, sizing the thigh and shin radii, and shaping a foot box that sits flush with the floor at y=0. I'm also considering knee plate details and how the pelvis height relates to leg length.

Now I'm checking the leg proportions so the hip-to-ankle distance comes out nearly straight with the knee bowed slightly forward, then moving to the head: using a scaled icosahedron for a chunky rounded rock-like head and positioning the neck joints to connect it to the torso.

Next I'm working out the jaw as a separate joint under the head with a glowing interior and small obsidian teeth spikes, then thinking about the eyes as glowing slit shapes to give the golem a simple anime-inspired face.

Computing where the eye planes should sit on the curved head ellipsoid surface...

I'm placing decal textures for the eyes onto the head mesh at the computed mirrored positions, then adding glow to the decal material. Next I want to add horn-like obsidian crystal spikes curving up from the head.

For the crest I'm planning five spikes along the head with orange-glowing tips, plus two larger curved horns swept via bezier curves and bound to the head bone with gold rings around them. Then I'm thinking through the back design: a spine ridge of spikes, glowing cracks, shoulder pauldrons, and skipping a floating halo in favor of grounded gold ornaments like a belt, collar, and hanging tassels built from small svg cards.

Now I'm working out the belt geometry as a closed catmull-rom sweep around the waist, picking radius and depth values that interpolate between the pelvis and hip proportions, binding it to the hips joint, and adding a glowing gold buckle gem out front before moving on to the loincloth.

For the basalt skin, I'm layering mottled color paints with cel-shading and a scales texture, nesting multiple purple-gray tones and defining how the shader resolves lit versus shadowed color based on the light angle threshold.

Now I'm designing a crack paint that uses cell-distance edges to pick bright orange or deep red-orange where the cracks are thin, falling back to the rock texture elsewhere, so the lava fissures read as glowing seams across the body and plates.

I'm defining the remaining palette: a toon-shaded gold using a cel pair of warm tones, obsidian with dark purple-blue cel shading, and a flat glow orange for exposed crystal. I need to keep the overall color and triangle count within budget, so I'm sketching a plate-placement helper to scatter armor segments efficiently.

Writing scatter logic for torso plates...

Still adjusting torso path and chest joint position... now working out pauldron geometry and placement, attaching them to shoulder joints so they move with the arms, plus adding a gold rim trim detail.

Then I'm positioning spikes and glow cracks on the pauldrons, and mapping out the arm's shoulder-elbow-wrist-fist chain with coordinates that keep proportions matching the torso width.

For the fist I'm building it from a scaled icosahedron plus knuckle boxes, looping through finger segments with spacing offsets and a thumb capsule, then adding an elbow spike with a gold ring accent and a bracer torus along the arm chain.

Working out the forearm radius taper, I'm defining a function that shrinks from upper arm to elbow then widens toward the wrist for a golem-like look, and placing a gold cuff torus sized to match that radius at the forearm.

Now I'm setting up the leg geometry with hip, knee, and ankle points on each side, plus a radius function that tapers the thigh down to the knee and flares slightly toward the ankle, along with a knee plate shaped from a scaled icosahedron.

Adding shin, foot, and toe geometry...

I'm adding a glowing seam ring at the thigh using a thin torus positioned slightly outside the leg's radius so it floats just above the skin surface. Now I'm working on head details, adding a lower jaw box positioned beneath the head ellipsoid to form a chin.

Good enough, moving head center up to 2.7. For teeth I'll add small cones along the jaw plus two larger upward tusk spikes with gold tips, and for the brow I'll angle a box above each eye tilted downward toward the center to give an angry expression.

Now I'm sketching the eye as an SVG decal: a sharp-angled polygon in bright yellow-orange representing the eye shape, with a darker slit polygon inside for the pupil, then I'll mirror this for the opposite side.

Good, so no mirroring needed for s=1 since model-left matches viewer's right already. I'm placing the decal target directly on the head part's surface, then working out horn geometry with a bezier sweep from base to tip, tapering the radius down to a point. I'll skip glowing tips and rings for now and consider adding a small gold torus band near the horn base instead.

Then I'm adding a row of crest spikes down the back of the skull using a spike helper function, spacing their bases and directions along the skull curve to keep the overall height near 3.3 meters for that "golem towers" feel. I'm also planning a glowing orange magma vent cluster on the back plus plate details, and defining seam cracks as polylines draped against the torso surface using nearest-point projection.

I'm working through how plates and seams interact -- since plates protrude slightly above the skin, I'm adjusting lift and sweep radius for the seam cracks so they ride realistically between or over the plates, treating them visually as molten fissures running through the plating. I'm sweeping the draped seam paths with a thin glowing lava-colored tube, picking a small palette of lava, hot, and ember tones for the glow accents.

I'm also adding flame-shaped card textures as glowing wisps on the shoulders, head crest, and back vents -- orienting the flame frames upward to face away from the body, positioning tufts at the crest and pauldron tops, then scattering a batch of small floating glowing embers around the figure so nothing looms directly overhead while keeping the lowest points grounded.

I'm cutting the embers down to a tighter cluster near the shoulders and arms, then adding gold-and-red tassels at the belt front using flipped card frames so they hang correctly, and starting on a gold filigree decal for the chest plate.

I realize the flat plane won't hug the curved chest surface evenly — at the edges it'd float several centimeters away. Better to decal the filigree texture directly onto the torso geometry instead of using a separate floating plane.

Then I add the glow core sphere and gold ring on top, slightly lifted above the decal surface. For the filigree SVG itself, I'm sketching a radial design with concentric circles and petal-shaped paths in gold stroke, sized to project cleanly onto the chest.

Now I'm planning the gold trim details — a collar sweep around the neck base matching the torso's shoulder curvature, plus belt, cuffs, and pauldron rim accents, while skipping decorative studs to keep things simpler. I still need to wire in the SVG and glow texture imports and set up a helper for left/right arm symmetry before writing the main component code.

Writing arm chains loop...

Faceted hex columns with sides:6, smooth:false would look great for basalt limbs, keeping torso loft at sides:8 smooth:false with cracked rock paint, and head as a flattened icosahedron ellipsoid.

For the pelvis I'm adding three hanging loincloth plates as small tilted boxes attached near the hip bone, then double-checking that only the actually used imports remain—THREE, createBuilder, frame, rng, catmull, bezier, paint, cells, mottle, scales—so nothing trips the unused-locals lint rule.

I'm scattering a handful of floating ember octahedrons around the chest using random angles and radii so they orbit the torso without clipping into it, then setting up a torus seam at the arm's 30% point along its chain for a ring detail.

Writing PLATE flat array...

Positioning pauldron spikes and dorsal spines...

Settling the rim detailing. I'll add scattered armor plates on thighs and forearms for richness, keeping the part count manageable, then write everything out in the Genshin Impact aesthetic style.
